ai.description: This lizard reaches 20 cm in length. It features a brownish body with dark spots and a vibrant orange-yellow throat fan. Distinctive lateral skin folds (patagia) allow gliding between trees.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable cue is the presence of a distinct, black-spotted yellow throat fan (dewlap) in males, which lacks the dark transverse bands found in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Draco dussumieri* inhabits the evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Southern Flying Lizard is primarily diurnal, using its patagium to glide between trees to forage for ants and termites while avoiding ground-based predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Draco dussumieri* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 2–5 eggs in a soil burrow. Breeding typically occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (February–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Draco dussumieri* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring from southern Gujarat through Maharashtra, Karnataka, and Kerala at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
